caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular wooden chest with a lid, rendered in shades of brown. The front of the chest is divided into three main panels, each with intricate carved designs. The two outer panels feature symmetrical carvings resembling stylized trees or large leafy plants set against an arched frame. The central panel displays a more complex pattern that includes foliage-like motifs flanking a central symmetrical element that appears floral in nature. Vertical carved strips resembling leafy vines separate each of the three front panels, as well as border the edges of the chest. Along the top edge, there is a horizontal band decorated with a repeated swirling pattern. Below the panels, a horizontal band features a sequence of geometric and floral carvings. The chest stands on four short legs, with the front legs and lower edge including additional carved decorative elements. The sides of the chest appear plain and unadorned except for visible wood grain. The chest is shown at a slight angle, revealing the front and left side. The background is plain and neutral.
title: Chest
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
